item.title: Nigeria’s creator economy may finally be coming of age
item.description: Nigeria’s creator economy is maturing, with creators earning meaningful income and platforms multiplying, signalling a growing and vibrant digital ecosystem.

item.title: Amazon plans satellite Internet launch in South Africa
item.description: On today's Techpoint Digest, we discuss Amazon's plans to launch satellite Internet in South Africa, Nigerian startups paying creators ₦15 billion in one year, and South Africa's plans to regulate podcasts.

item.title: Paystack creates holding company, The Stack Group, turns profitable, and bets on AI
item.description: Paystack says it is now profitable as it launches The Stack Group, a new holding company that brings together its payments, banking, and AI ambitions

item.title: Google Report: Nigeria leads rest of the world in AI for learning, 26% above global average
item.description: The result revealed that 88% of Nigerian adults use AI chatbots for various reasons, including education, business, and entrepreneurship.

item.title: Indian defence player targets Africa to boost country’s exports
item.description: Tata is expanding into Africa as India pushes defence exports, opening a Morocco factory and pursuing military hardware deals with regional governments.

item.title: After 3 startup shutdowns, this founder built Africa’s biggest Web3 incubation programme
item.description: Eric Annan bought bitcoin at $354, but after losing all his crypto earnings to failed businesses, the lessons he learned led him to build Aya HQ, one of Africa's biggest Web3 incubation programmes.

item.title: Congo eyes new subsea cable to fix Internet disruptions
item.description: On today's Techpoint Digest, we discuss Congo's plans for a new subsea cable to address Internet disruptions, X, and Paystack's evolution beyond a payments company.

item.title: Do African VCs really lack conviction, or are they playing a different game?
item.description: Terra Industries’ seed round reignited claims that African VCs lack ambition, but a closer look suggests the story is less about fear and more about structural constraints.

item.title: Egypt ends duty-free mobile phone exemption for incoming passengers
item.description: Egypt has scrapped the duty-free phone allowance for travelers, citing booming local manufacturing. The move, effective Wednesday, has sparked criticism from lawmakers concerned about its impact on expatriates.

item.title: From ₦36k to CEO: Jane Egerton-Idehen on building wealth through tech careers
item.description: Jane Egerton-Idehen started in tech earning ₦36k as a corps member, running 24/7 satellite shifts for extra pay. Now MD/CEO of NIGCOMSAT, she advises: chase challenging opportunities and skills first, financial growth will follow.
